Notes: Year Established -925 = Judahite Maresha: 2 Chr 11:8 lists Mareshah among the cities fortified by Rehoboam (conventional date c. 925 BCE; biblical date, historicity of the list debated); Josh 15:44 places it in Judah; excavations show 8th-6th c. BCE Judahite fortifications. This row: c. 586 BCE (6th-c. campaign of Nebuchadnezzar II) 'marked the end of Maresha as a Judahite city'; Edomites then migrated into the area and Maresha became a major Idumean city. Population blank: end of Judahite rule, not a stated total absence of Judahites. (Wikipedia used as last resort.)

Exilic period (586-539 BCE; midpoint used, c.): BAS timeline 'Maresha Through the Years' states 'The Jewish population of the site is probably assimilated by the Edomites' as the Edomites expanded into southern Judah (Idumea). Iron Age II: 'Israelites settle in Maresha'; walls and fortifications of the 8th-6th c. BCE in the upper city. Probable assimilation, not documented absence, so Population blank. The same page gives a Hellenistic total population of 6,000-10,000 for this Idumean (non-Jewish) city - not entered as Jewish population.

Late Persian period Idumaea (4th c. BCE; midpoint used, c.): Shatzman (SCI 32, 2013, n. 99) writes that 'Jews were settled in Idumaea, perhaps 10 percent of the entire population, as may be inferred from a study of about 1300 personal names recovered from inscriptions and ostraca (Kloner and Stern 2007, 142-3)' - the cited study is 'Idumea in the Late Persian Period (Fourth Century B.C.E.)'. REGIONAL figure for Idumaea (of which Marisa was the chief city), not a count for Marisa, so Population blank; it suggests a Judean minority in the district. Shatzman applies it to the Ptolemaic period (Zenon papyri, mid-3rd c. BCE; official Alexandros resided in Marisa) and adds that 1 Macc 5:1-3 probably implies Judean presence in Idumaea.

Hellenistic Maresha (3rd-2nd c. BCE; midpoint used, c.): BAS (Bible History Daily, 2013) - Maresha 'expanded greatly in the third century B.C.E.'; its subterranean complexes served 'a multi-ethnic community of Idumeans, Judeans and Arabs', and hundreds of ostraca in Aramaic, Greek and Hebrew from the caves contain more than 1,300 personal names from the city's Idumean, Judean and Arab population. Documents Judean residents in the Idumean-dominated city; no count or share given.

Hellenistic Marisa (2nd c. BCE, c.): Encyclopaedia Judaica (M. Avi-Yonah) - a Sidonian colony settled there and it served as an administrative centre; 'Its population, however, was mostly Edomite', and it served as a base for the Seleucid armies at war with Judah Maccabee, who ravaged its territory (Maccabean campaigns, c. 163 BCE); 'the inscriptions indicate a gradual assimilation of the Sidonians into the Idumean and Jewish populations there' (Sidonian tomb inscriptions, late 3rd-2nd c. BCE). Indicates a Jewish component in the town's population; whether it predates or follows the Hasmonean conquest is not specified. No count.

Hasmonean conquest and Judaization (c. 112 BCE): Josephus, Antiquities 13.257-258 (9.1): 'Hyrcanus took also Dora and Marissa, cities of Idumea, and subdued all the Idumeans; and permitted them to stay in that country, if they would circumcise their genitals, and make use of the laws of the Jews' - they submitted to circumcision 'and the rest of the Jewish ways of living'. Ancient literary source; the remaining Idumean inhabitants became Judeans by conversion. No figure.

Date and aftermath of the conquest (c. 108/107 BCE): Shatzman (2013) - coins, funerary inscriptions, weights and stamped amphora handles show Marisa 'was not captured before 112/111'; he argues it fell in 108/107 or soon after. Coin evidence (5 post-conquest foreign coins vs 856 pre-conquest; very few Jannaeus coins) 'is patent evidence that Marisa ceased to be settled a short time after the conquest of John Hyrcanus, although it is possible that a Hasmonaean garrison had briefly occupied the site'. Kloner too concluded the city was abandoned rather than systematically destroyed. Garrison size unknown; Population blank.

Documented abandonment (first half of 1st c. BCE; midpoint used, c.): Shatzman (2013) - 'All in all the archaeological finds show that Marisa was not occupied in the first half of the first century'; 'Marisa was abandoned after its capture by John Hyrcanus, and Tel Sandahanna was not occupied in the first century'. The Gabinian city (c. 58/57 BCE) was probably at Beth Guvrin c. 2 km north (Qedar, Kloner). Population 0 refers to the site of Tel Maresha. Contrast Wikipedia, which says the site 'remained sparsely populated' until 40 BCE.

Pompey's settlement (63 BCE): Josephus, Antiquities 14.75 (4.4) - Pompey restored Hippos, Scythopolis, Pella, Dios, Samaria, 'as also Marissa, and Ashdod, and Jamnia, and Arethusa, to their own inhabitants', i.e. Marisa was detached from Hasmonean Judean rule. Event; no Jewish figure.

Re-foundation under Gabinius (57-55 BCE, c.): Josephus, Antiquities 14.88 (5.3) - Samaria, Ashdod, Scythopolis, Anthedon, Raphia, Dora, 'Marissa also, and Gaza' were rebuilt; 'these cities were securely inhabited, which had been desolate for a long time'. Re-founded as a non-Jewish polis (Gabinian city coins); no Jewish figure.

Destruction by the Parthians (40 BCE): Josephus, Antiquities 14.364 (13.9) - not content with plundering Jerusalem, the Parthians 'went out into the country, and plundered it, and demolished the city Marissa' (parallel War 1.269). After this the site was abandoned (per Wikipedia and EJ). Event; Population blank (Jewish residents at that time not documented).

1st c. CE (midpoint used, c.): Weitzman (HTR 92, 1999, n. 12) notes 'a tomb from the first century CE found in the necropolis of the Idumean site of Marisa' with 'a burial performed in a style common in Jerusalem and other sites of Jewish habitation', but 'it is unclear whether this tomb was used by converted Idumeans or by Jewish refugees from Judea'; the name 'Absalom' on a necropolis inscription is 'no less ambiguous'. Possible Jewish (Judean or Judaized Idumean) burial in the Marisa / Beth Guvrin area; single tomb, scale unknown. No count.
